claims.text: High-temperature oxidation resistance and material integrity in MPEAs are governed by formation of a self-healing mixed-oxide scale.
The protective mixed-oxide scale forms through selective surface segregation of oxide-forming elements such as Cr or Al.
Lattice distortions inherent in the MPEA matrix stabilize the protective oxide scale.
MPEA lattice distortions slow oxygen diffusion and metal-cation mobility.
Reduced oxygen and cation mobility produces a slow-growing, adherent oxide scale that protects the underlying alloy.
The proposed starting material is a polycrystalline, single-phase MPEA with a homogeneous elemental distribution in the as-cast or annealed state.
Increasing the concentration of a key oxide-forming element will promote formation of a nanocrystalline, continuous mixed-oxide scale enriched in that element.
Selective surface segregation creates a localized composition favorable for protective oxide phases.
Diffusion barriers created by lattice distortion make oxide growth self-limiting.
A self-limiting, adherent oxide scale preserves the mechanical integrity of the bulk alloy during high-temperature exposure.
Relative to a lower-Cr or lower-Al baseline, an enhanced-Cr or enhanced-Al variant will develop a thinner oxide scale.
Relative to the baseline, the enhanced oxide-former variant will exhibit lower oxidation mass-gain rates.
Relative to the baseline, the enhanced oxide-former variant will form a more uniform and better-adhered scale with less porosity and spallation.
The proposed baseline has rapid oxidation behavior, including higher mass gain and a thicker, less-adherent oxide scale.
The proposed mechanism should remain operative during prolonged exposure at approximately 1000–1100 °C provided the alloy does not undergo phase separation or other drastic microstructural changes.

Failure of the enhanced oxide-former variant to show statistically significantly lower mass gain, reduced scale thickness, and improved adhesion and uniformity would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
